title: Integral section injectivity at a closed geometric point of a strictly henselian base
statement: Let A be a strictly henselian local ring, Lambda a commutative ring, p:Z -> Spec A an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and F an etale sheaf of Lambda-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For an algebraically closed field Omega and t:Spec Omega -> Spec A with image the closed point, let (i:Z' -> Z,p':Z' -> Spec Omega,p,t) be Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Then the canonical inverse-image unit map on global sections Gamma(Z,F) -> Gamma(Z',i^*F) is injective. No finite-type, torsion, or nonempty-fibre assumption is made.

source.place: Tags 09XK, 09ZH and 0A3I; henselian degree-zero consequence used for the integral comparison

proof.text: Since p is integral and the base is affine, write Z as Spec B for an integral A-algebra B using the canonical affine presentation. Set J=m_A B. Apply the integral-over-henselian-pair theorem to obtain HenselianRing B J.
Apply the degree-zero comparison to the proper identity of Spec B and the quotient map B -> B/J. It makes restriction of F to the closed fibre an isomorphism on sections. This also covers B=0.

The closed-image condition on t says that the corresponding A -> Omega map kills m_A, hence factors through k=A/m_A. This is a field embedding, with k separably closed. Identify Z′ with the extension of the closed fibre along k -> Omega. Apply the base-field-extension section comparison and the canonical module/set inverse-image comparison, with its unit equation, to get bijectivity on module sections.

Composition of inverse-image units, transported through the affine presentation and pullback isomorphism, identifies the displayed global-section map with the two successive restrictions. The composition formula on global sections makes this identification explicit. Compose the two injective maps.
